open_decisions.summary: A blade or modal traps focus while open. Measurement now confirms the implementation's argument: a modal traps (HeadlessUI); a maximized blade does NOT trap but everything it covers is inert, and Shift+Tab from its first focusable exits the document rather than reaching hidden content, so 2.4.3/4.1.2 hold and 2.1.2 (Level A) is not violated. The AC as written still says the opposite. Needs a ruling from the accessibility-conformance owner, then AC-4 should be rewritten to the outcome. This is why the verdict is PASS_WITH_NOTES rather than PASS. Nothing filed.

VCST-5814.evidence: detached-opener variant lands on main (the declared workspace fallback), 3/3, exactly where a prior run recorded <body>

VCST-5815.evidence: app-hub popover 4 axe hits -> 0 under a maximized blade; notifications node present -> absent

measurement_notes: AC-3b required the scoped axe A/B, NOT the ARIA snapshot: the snapshot lists the sidebar with full accessible names in BOTH states and would have manufactured a false PASS. Sidebar applicable rules 23 (restored) -> 2 (maximized), with 21 content-dependent rules going inapplicable and back.

The literal 'popup opened while focus already loose' path is unreachable as written: a mouse click on a button focuses it, so the opener is never absent. The real fallback was reached via the unsaved-changes dialog, which detaches the opener on confirm.

Backdrop dismiss BLOCKED for the third consecutive run: browser_click targets element centres only and every dialog ancestor is viewport-centred, so the centre resolves inside the panel (Playwright reported the interception explicitly). Tried 1920x1080, 1920x300 to shift the centre, axe-derived overlay selectors rather than guessed ones, and 390x844 where the mobile variant has no backdrop at all. No coordinate/offset-click primitive exists in this MCP server.
